chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Dawud ibn Farqad or Qutaybah al-A'sha, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, may our fathers and mothers be sacrificed for you. Indeed, the people of kindness (al-ma'ruf) in the world were known by their kindness, so by what will they be known in the Hereafter?' He said: 'Indeed, when Allah, Blessed and High, brings the people of Paradise into Paradise, He commands a sweet, fragrant wind, which clings to the people of kindness. So no one among them passes by a group of the people of Paradise except that they find their scent, so they say, 'This one is from the people of kindness.'
ai.seo_question: How are people of kindness recognized in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the eschatological reward for consistent benevolence, describing a divine fragrance that clings to the doers of good as a permanent mark of their character. This physical manifestation of spiritual virtue underscores the Shia concept that good deeds leave an indelible trace on the soul, transforming the individual into a recognizable beacon of righteousness even among the multitude of Paradise.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from zakariyya Al Momin, from Dawood Bin Farqad, or Quteyba Al A’asha,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The companions of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! May our fathers and our mothers be sacrificed for you<sup>saww</sup>! The performers of the acts of kindness in the world are known for their acts of kindness, so how will they be known in the Hereafter?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Enters the people of the Paradise into the Paradise, would Command a misty aromatic wind, so it would affix itself to the people (performers) of the acts of kindness. Thus, not one of them would pass by a group from the inhabitants of the Paradise except that they would find its aroma, so they would say, ‘This one is from the people (performer) of the acts of kindness’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Zakariya al-Mu’min from Dawud ibn Farqad or Qutaybah al-A‘sha’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated this Hadith. ‘Once, companions of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, asked a question. “O Messenger of Allah, we pray to Allah to keep our souls and the souls of ancestors in service for your cause; if people who provide Benevolent Assistance are recognized because of such acts, by what means will they be recognized on the Day of Judgment?”

He (the Messenger of Allah) replied, “When Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, will admit providers of Benevolent Assistance in Paradise, He will command a wind that carries a certain fragrance to accompany them. Whenever one of them passes by the people in Paradise, they notice the fragrance and say, ‘This is one of the providers of benevolent assistance.”””
